steps.message:
# Some coins misbehave in the flooded cave

### What happens
`recording.mp4` is an uncut run through a flooded cave basin. Partway through the clip, Tux does something that releases a group of new coins. From that moment until the end of the clip, those coins do not behave the way coins in this game should. The coins that were already placed in the level, Tux, the fish and the scenery in the recording are correct.

### Expected
The released coins should behave like a normal coin burst in this game, from the moment they spread out of the block until they come to rest and Tux swims back to collect them. Once a coin is in the water it should drift down slowly. Fix every way the released coins behave wrongly in the recording.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` (44 seconds)

You can inspect individual moments of the video by extracting frames from it with `ffmpeg`.

Inspect the attached file before making changes.

steps.message:
I couldn't watch the recording: `/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty and there's no `recording.mp4` anywhere on the system. So these fixes come from reading the code that runs when a coin block bursts (`CoinExplode` → `HeavyCoin`), not from the video. The game builds with the changes, but I haven't played it to check the result on screen.

I found four bugs in the released coins:

1. **The spread was mirrored up/down instead of left/right** (`src/object/coin_explode.cpp`). The left/right sign was applied to the vertical speed. Half the coins were shot downward and none went left. Now each pair fans out to both sides and every coin starts moving upward.

2. **Coins never settled** (`HeavyCoin::collision_solid` in `src/object/coin.cpp`).
   - Any landing faster than 20 made the coin bounce back up at 99, so it landed fast enough to bounce again, forever. A coin now bounces only when it lands faster than 200.
   - When a coin stopped bouncing, its sideways speed was never cleared, so it slid along the floor. Landing now stops it completely so it comes to rest.

3. **Tux couldn't collect them** (`HeavyCoin` constructors). The released coins were in a collision group that only touches walls and floors, so swimming back through them did nothing. They're now in the normal moving group. The rock code already has a special case for these coins, which only matters if they're in that group.

4. **They ignored water** (`HeavyCoin::update`). The coins fell at full speed underwater. They now use the same water handling as the rock: gravity drops to 20%, and their movement slows to 40% sideways and 60% downward, so they drift down slowly.

If you can provide the recording, I can check these four fixes against it.
